questions.q: Under the lesson's traffic-light rules, where can Amber (internal) information go?
options: Into any AI tool, as long as people's names are removed first
Nowhere, unless a written exception has been approved
Into personal AI accounts that only the owner uses
Only into approved business-grade tools with training turned off
questions.explain: The lesson says Amber information, such as internal processes and unpublished pricing, goes only in business-grade tools the company has approved, with training on its data turned off.

questions.q: The office manager at a cleaning company wants AI's help replying to a customer who was charged twice. What does the lesson recommend?
options: Paste the full email thread and ask the AI to strip out personal details
Describe the situation without names, contact details or account numbers
Paste the customer's details, since a reply email is low risk
Avoid AI entirely, because billing complaints can't be drafted with it
questions.explain: The lesson says to anonymize before you paste, rather than pasting raw data and asking AI to clean it up, because by then it has already been shared; a described scenario still gets an excellent reply.

questions.q: A consultancy connects its AI assistant to its inbox so the AI can work with incoming emails. Which safeguard does the lesson recommend?
options: A human approval step before any AI action that sends, deletes, pays or shares
Letting the AI act freely, but only on emails from known senders
Removing the business context pack while the inbox is connected
Telling the AI to ignore any instructions it finds in the emails
questions.explain: Outside content can include instructions designed to steer the AI (prompt injection), so the lesson's safeguard is a human approval step before any AI action that sends, deletes, pays for or shares anything.
